content:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: high error rate (503) on /v1/generate in eu-west-1 · 86% of requests failing · paging maya (oncall)
Maya: on it, pulling up dashboards. can someone confirm if this is region-wide or model-specific? :eyes:
Sam: i'm seeing elevated 5xx across both fastgen and standard routes in eu-west-1, spike started ~03:12 UTC
Maya: thanks. attaching request samples and logs in a sec. i'm going to mute non-critical alerts and start mitigation checklist.
Leo: FYI i'm jumping in to assist on routing/fallbacks. hit me with traffic percentages per model when you have them.
Maya: quick ps: statuspage draft link -> https://redwood.statuspage.io/incident-drafts/INC-2866 (do not publish yet)
Sam: traffic snapshot: fastgen=48%, standard=42%, embeddings=10%. error traces show 503 from inference-runtime pod pool eu-gen-03.
Maya: rolling restart of eu-gen-03 in progress (kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-runtime -n eu). will watch logs.
Maya: logs show OOMKilled on several workers, also "kvcache shard failed to initialize" in the same window.
Frank: comms checklist: we need initial statuspage message ASAP — short impact, region, mitigation steps. i'll draft but need confirmation of customer impact (SLA?).
Rita: Ops note: Dedicated customers in eu may be routed to backup region per routing policy; default fallback is eu-south->eu-north then us-east.
Maya: rollout completed, restarting failed pods one by one to avoid thundering herd. current pod count stabilizing at 8/10 then 10/10.
Sam: after restart: error rate dropped to ~6% in last 2 minutes. latency slightly elevated.
Maya: mitigation step 1 successful (pod restart). moving to step 2: investigate root cause — looks like a memory regression in recent runtime 2.14.2 image.
Leo: can we confirm if image 2.14.2 was rolled to eu-gen-03? deployment history shows a canary 2.14.2 pushed 02:45 UTC, full rollout to eu-gen-xx at 03:00 UTC.
Maya: yes, 2.14.2 is suspect. opening a rollback to 2.14.1 on eu clusters now: kubectl set image deploy/inference-runtime=redwood/runtime:2.14.1 -n eu && kubectl rollout status deploy/inference-runtime -n eu
deploy-bot: Rollout initiated for deploy/inference-runtime to image redwood/runtime:2.14.1 (eu).
Sam: rollback in flight, monitoring metrics.
Maya: statuspage draft updated by frank. Copy suggestion below — please approve or edit quickly.
Frank: DRAFT (for statuspage initial):
"Start time: 2026-03-15T03:12:00Z
Summary: Users in the EU region may have experienced elevated error rates and failed requests to text generation endpoints (HTTP 503) due to a regression in the inference runtime after a recent image rollout.
Impact: Customers using hosted API in eu-west-1 may have experienced failures or degraded throughput. Dedicated customers may have experienced fallback routing.
Mitigation: We have rolled back the runtime image to a previous stable version, restarted affected pods, and traffic has returned toward normal. We will continue monitoring and will provide follow-up updates.
Status: Investigating -> Mitigating"
Maya: minor edits: add ETA for follow-up: "Next update within 30 minutes" and add no action required for most customers; only those with strict on-prem routing may need to reconfigure.
Frank: updated. Also adding link to support KB: https://support.redwood.com/kb/known-issues/2866-runtime-regression
Rita: heads-up for enterprise CSMs: notify top 10 EU customers with private instances; they might need to check dedicated routing policies.
Leo: ops suggestion: add technical note that root cause likely memory leak introduced in 2.14.2 when handling long-context requests — under reproducer creation.
Maya: agreed. frank — can you publish initial statuspage now? we have rollback under way and error rate dropping.
Frank: publishing initial update now. publishing content: see link in draft. :rocket:
Frank: STATUSPAGE PUBLISHED: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2866 (Initial update posted)
Maya: good. switching to customer impact assessment: estimated affected requests ~0.7% of total daily tokens for eu region; some enterprise requests retried by clients; SLA exposure possible for sustained failures during window.
Sam: creating incident timeline snippet for postmortem. will add logs and pod events.
Rita: CSM outreach: i'll coordinate email template for top customers, include mitigation steps and offer a post-incident review.
Frank: preparing the periodic update template. Suggested cadence: 30m, 2h, 6h until resolved. Next update scheduled at 03:40 UTC.
Maya: can we add a short internal note about rollback gating and release freeze for 2.14.x until root cause confirmed?
Leo: yes, marking release freeze and blocking any automatic promotion pipelines: disabling automated rollout in eu pools and opening an RIT (release incident tracking) entry.
Maya: internal checklist posted in thread:
- Confirm rollback completed ✅
- Monitor 5xx for 30m post-rollback (in progress) ⏳
- Notify CSMs for dedicated customers (assigned to Rita) ✉️
- Publish initial statuspage (done) :white_check_mark:
- Prepare customer email and support KB (Frank/Rita) ✍️
- Create postmortem timeline (Sam) 🧾
Sam: all items acknowledged. I'll take the postmortem and timeline notes.
Frank: posted customer-friendly short note for CSM/email team: "We observed elevated failures to the hosted inference API in EU. We rolled back a recent runtime image that caused the issue and service is returning to normal. If you see persistent errors please reply to this thread or contact support@redwood.ai."
Maya: good. will keep thread updated. next update: 03:40 UTC or earlier if status changes.
deploy-bot: Rollout completed: inference-runtime -> redwood/runtime:2.14.1 (eu)
Sam: metrics update: 5xx now <1% over last 5m, avg latency +40ms above baseline.
Maya: marking current state as "Mitigated". moving to root cause analysis.
Frank: scheduling resolved notice draft for statuspage once we're stable for 2 hours. I'll prepare language and link to postmortem when ready.
Rita: CSM outreach in progress, checking in with top customers — none reporting ongoing issues as of 03:55 UTC.
Maya: thanks all. closing on-call handoff note: I'll follow up in postmortem and add recommendations (memory guardrails, stronger canary policies).
Frank: RESOLVE DRAFT: "We have resolved the incident by rolling back to a stable runtime image. Service is operating normally. No further action required for most customers. We will publish a full post-incident report within 5 business days."
Maya: looks good. file saved to incident tracker and moving to post-incident review.
Frank: final publish of resolved notice scheduled if metrics remain stable for 2 hours.
Maya: thread closing, thanks everyone. :pray:"
